timeline.title: Ninh Binh
description: Experience the outstanding natural beauty and iconic history of Ninh Binh in this full-day tour. After collection from the Hanoi hotel, enjoy a scenic drive to an area of natural beauty, often referred to as ‘Ha Long Bay on land’. Once there, meander lazily down the tranquil Ngo Dong river - pass kayakers and daredevil swimmers en route to the ancient Tam Coc or ‘Three Caves’. Gaze in awe as foliage-topped limestone cliffs loom magnificently over the tranquil waters – don’t forget to take a camera to this stunning natural wonder.

Disembark the vessel and take a short trek to experience the quiet beauty of Thai Vi temple. Built in 1258 by King Tran Thai Tong to worship Buddha and the three saints, this stunning example of ancient architecture has an undeniable air of peace and tranquility. Constructed from monolithic greenstone and boasting unique features such as pagodas, stone carvings and more, Thai Vi is a place that will not be easily forgotten. After time to explore and unwind, walk through electric green rice paddies to a secluded local restaurant surrounded by limestone mountains and lakes to enjoy a selection of local delicacies.

Once sated, continue the exploration of these magical lands. Walk to the village of Van Lam Hamlet, known for its traditional lace embroidery practices. Meet with smiling locals and hear how they preserve this 700-year-old craft in modern times. Come away with a small embroidery gift and transfer back to Hanoi with wonderful memories of this special place.

timeline.title: Ho Chi Minh City Tour
description: Start your day visiting two iconic architectural landmarks the Notre Dame Cathedral and the Central Post Office built between 1877 and 1883 by renowned designer Gustav Eiffel. The cathedral still remains an active church with services each day and is favoured backdrop for Vietnamese wedding photographs.

From the cathedral, take a short stroll along Dong Khoi Street to the Opera House. From a bomb shelter to housing the parliamentary Lower House, the Opera House has had an interesting history. Restored in 1995 the Opera House has returned to its roots and is once again a theatre.

Next, visit the Reunification Palace, once a symbol of the South Vietnamese Government. It was here on 30 April 1975, that the war ended when a North Vietnamese Army tank crashed through its gates. See the war room, the banquet hall and the presidential office with the unusual gifts which have been received. In the afternoon continue on to the War Remnants Museum. Here, your guide will tell the story of the city’s darkest and most tragic hours during the Vietnam War. The museum contains displays of military aircraft, weaponry and many photographs – some that are quite graphic in nature

Head to Cho Lon - the city’s Chinatown and Thien Hau Pagoda which is dedicated to the Goddess of the Sea. With intricate friezes, carved tableaus and impressive incense coils make for some great photos. Then observe street life with a cyclo ride through the narrow streets to Binh Tay market that sells everything from hats to dried squid!

Note: Binh Tay market, an 88 year old structure is going under a comprehensive 365-day-restoration project starting from Nov 2016. During this renovation time, the visit will be arranged at temporary market, located on Thap Muoi Street, just opposite the existing market, with space for up to 1,077 stalls.

timeline.title: Hoa Lu and Trang An Day Tour
description: Your guide and driver will meet you at 8:30am. You will then embark on a journey south of about 100 kilometres to Hoa Lu, the ancient capital of the Dinh and Le dynasties dating back to the 11th century. Having been eroded over the millennia, the dilapidated ruins have nearly been absorbed by the spectacular scenery creating a mystical atmosphere that will be sure to titillate your imagination.

After lunch in a local restaurant you will continue to nearby Trang An, a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its outstanding natural beauty and the scenic karst formations which contribute to its reputation as being the “Halong Bay on land.” Board a small boat and meander lazily down the peaceful river while passing through a series of caves. While enjoying the sounds of soaring birds overhead and paddling along the crystal-clear waters of the river, jagged limestone hills jutting skyward out of electric green rice paddies will be sure to bring out the photographer in you.
Finally, return to the pier, where your vehicle will be waiting for you, and arrive back in Hanoi in the late afternoon.

Home to some of the country’s most striking historical architecture, this former trading port once welcomed Chinese, Dutch, French, Japanese, Portuguese and Arab merchants and this varied cultural influence is still very much evident today.Begin the walking tour through the charming streets lined with honey-yellow buildings until reaching Chua Ong Pagoda. This ancient, Chinese-inspired structure dates back to 1653, and within its walls, visitors can smell the sweet aroma of incense. From here, walk onward to nearby Phuc Kien Assembly Hall and Jinshang Temple, dedicated to the Goddess of the Sea.After taking in the fascinating 200-year-old Tan Ky House, enjoy a short rest at one of Hoi An’s most iconic structures, the beautiful and intricately decorated Japanese Covered Bridge. Next, relax with a revitalising cup of tea at Reaching Out Tea House - an establishment that aids members of the community who are living with disabilities. For lunch, witness a cookery demonstration of traditional Hoi An delicacies before enjoying the delectable meal.Once sated, head to Cam Thanh Village, a small community located on the outskirts of central Hoi An. Take a stroll to one of the traditional, diminutive village homes and meet a local family to learn about life in the community. On the neighbouring river, clamber into a bamboo basket boat and head to a water coconut forest before boarding a larger boat back to central Hoi An, gazing at the stunning canal side scenery. Complete this fun-filled day with a delicious cocktail at a rooftop bar.

timeline.title: Classic Cu Chi Tunnels Tour
description: Begin your journey to the Cu Chi Tunnels by departing at around 8am from your hotel and travel through the countryside which was once a stronghold of the Viet Cong. Upon arrival, watch a short video about what life was like for soldiers who lived there during the war. The cramped tunnels were central to a few of the war’s strategic operations, including the famous 1968 Tet Offensive, and they didn’t escape damage. American B52 bombers dropped hundreds of missiles leaving huge tell-tale craters behind. The tunnels served not only as living quarters, but as supply routes and hospitals for thousands of guerilla fighters. Many died there from malaria and other diseases, and a few were also born or married. Today they are viewed by some as a testimony to the Vietnamese people’s resiliency.
Return to Ho Chi Minh City 12.30 pm, just in time to enjoy a late lunch at your hotel.

timeline.title: Hidden Hanoi Walking Tour
description: Start the morning with a walk to the Northern Gate of the ancient citadel, a gargantuan fortress in the heart of the city. Learn a bit about the history of the imposing structure and visit Cua Bac Church, a beautiful example of French and catholic influence in the city.

Stroll along leafy Phan Dinh Phung Road, in the shade of the ancient dracontomelums trees lining one of Hanoi’s most romantic boulevards. Admire the magnificent French-colonial villas along the way before heading to Quan Thanh Temple. The 11th-century Taoist temple is one of the oldest and most culturally significant in the city.

Next, stroll toward West Lake and walk along the shore of the lake to Chau Long Market for a closer look at Hanoian culture in the flurry of a local market. After exploring the street stalls, set off along a quieter alley and take a short break at a local restaurant, sampling Pho Cuon, a delicious snack similar to fresh spring rolls.

Continue toward Hang Than Street, the epicentre of Hanoi’s thriving wedding cake stores. Learn a bit about Vietnam’s unique wedding culture and continue walking to the historic Long Bien Railway Station, located on the bridgehead of the impressive Long Bien Bridge.

Wrap up this captivating tour of Hanoi with a cyclo ride. Equal parts transportation and travel experience, these traditional bicycle rickshaws move at a leisurely pace that’s perfect for photos and slow-moving sightseeing. Sit back and relax whilst weaving through some of the Old Quarter’s busiest streets and end the tour with lunch at a local restaurant.

timeline.title: Cu Chi Tunnels by Saigon River
description: Depart from Ho Chi Minh City pier and begin your speedboat journey on the Saigon River. As the city fades into the background, observe life along the river and the many new ‘weekend’ homes being built by the Saigonese.

The cramped tunnels were central to a few of the war’s strategic operations, including the famous 1968 Tet Offensive, and they didn’t escape damage. American B52 bombers dropped hundreds of missiles leaving huge tell-tale craters behind. The tunnels also have “mantraps” – large camouflaged holes dug deep into the ground that ensnared enemy soldiers by bamboo spikes. But don’t worry, you won’t step in one! You’ll also discover the remains of an American tank that was destroyed by a landmine which you can climb on for great photos. The Cu Chi experience can be emotionally draining for some visitors, but it offers fascinating windows into the hardship and traumas of war.

Next, it’s a short drive through the countryside to visit a cricket farm. Some Vietnamese consider crickets a delicacy, and local lore says that hungry soldiers ate them to beef up their nutrient-poor diets. At the farm you’ll see crickets in various stages of growth. You’ll also have a chance to sample crickets wrapped up in tasty spring rolls. Make sure you snap a photograph so that your friends will believe your unusual tale! Stop for a traditional Vietnamese lunch – it won’t include cricket — en route to Ho Chi Minh City, arriving mid afternoon.

description: Go beyond the ordinary in beautiful Hoi An with a cycling journey into the city's idyllic rural outskirts. Set off from central Hoi An for a leisurely pedal out of town, weaving through rice paddy fields and along dusty country lanes bound for Cam Thanh Village. This charming community not far from Hoi An still boasts a timeless charm otherwise vanishing in other parts of Vietnam. Arrive at the home of a local family here and learn about their day-to-day lives in rural Vietnam.

Then, leave your bicycle behind and board a bamboo basket boat that local crab fishermen still use to haul in their daily catch. Learn the tricks behind the trade from friendly local fishing experts, and get a hands-on look at the livelihoods that keep this community thriving. Afterwards, take a well-earned rest with a fresh coconut water in hand, before cycling onward to Ha Linh lantern workshop. As one of the most iconic traditional crafts in Hoi An - so iconic that a monthly festival in the sleepy town revolves around lanterns and the full moon - learn how these delicate creations are made. Roll up your sleeves and make your own in a master class before heading back toward central Hoi An by bicycle.

timeline.title: The Story of Saigon
description: Start your Story of Saigon with a visit to the War Remnants Museum. Here, your guide will tell the story of the city’s darkest and most tragic hours during the Vietnam War. The museum contains displays of military aircraft, weaponry and many photographs – some that are quite graphic in nature. Although many of Vietnam’s 90 million people are now too young to remember the war, its legacy is still felt strongly across Vietnamese society.

Next, visit the Reunification Palace, once a symbol of the South Vietnamese Government. It was here on 30 April 1975, that the war ended when a North Vietnamese Army tank crashed through its gates. See the war room, the banquet hall and the presidential office with the unusual gifts which have been received. Then, continue to the Central Post Office, designed and constructed by the renowned architect Gustave Eiffel, and take a moment to send a postcard! Just behind the post office is the Notre Dame Cathedral, an iconic Saigon landmark built in neo-Romanesque style by the French between 1863 and 1880. Today it’s a favoured backdrop for Vietnamese wedding photographs.

Next, stroll down follow Dong Khoi Street, which figured prominently in Graham Greene’s famous Vietnam novel, The Quiet American, as Rue Catinat. The walk ends at the Saigon Opera House. From a bomb shelter to housing the parliamentary Lower House, the Opera House has had an interesting history.
End your day with a speedboat trip along the city’s ancient canals where life carries on unchanged. Return to your hotel as the sun sets on this fascinating city.

description: Discover a different side to the Vietnamese capital on this half-day tour of Hanoi’s charming countryside. From the passenger’s seat of a vintage Vespa, travel past the impressive Long Bien Bridge, leaving behind the traffic and commotion of the city. Spanning across the Red River, this cantilever bridge was built during French colonial times and became a symbol of courage and resilience of the Vietnamese people.

Whizz through the lush scenery until reaching the ancient Co Loa citadel. Once the national capital (AD 939 – 944), the spiral-shaped structure was the first fortified citadel in Vietnam and, despite only vestiges of the ancient ramparts remaining, is an important historical site.Next, follow some back roads and head to a local farm. Surrounded by nothing but lush rice paddies, learn about the rural lifestyle of the farmers before hitting the road again.

Enjoy the refreshing breeze and picturesque scenery whilst cruising through the valley and stop at a hidden wood carving village. Meet the local craftsmen and discover the ancient techniques used for producing traditional Buddhist statues.
Finish this outdoor adventure with a visit to a bustling market. Accompanied by a local family, peruse the different stalls and pick up a couple of delicious snacks before driving back to the city.

description: Start this cultural half-day tour of charming Hanoi at the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology. Be captivated by their stories and sample different types of tea before learning the secrets of brewing a delicious cup of the hot beverage.
After this marvellous experience, say goodbye to the passionate tea masters and travel back to the hotel, marking the end of this fascinating journey into Vietnamese culture.

timeline.title: Da Nang Discovery
description: Leave the hustle and bustle of Central Vietnam’s most frenetic city with a visit to the stunning Marble Mountains. Consisting of a cluster of five craggy marble and limestone cliffs, they were named to honour the five elements of earth, fire, water, metal and wood. During the unsettled years of the Vietnam War, these cliffs served as battlegrounds and hospitals. Explore the battle-scarred crevices before taking in the beauty of the Buddhist temples and statues that fill the wide caves. Discover and learn how this beautiful natural landmark has entrenched itself in the rich history of Vietnam.Next stop is the Son Tra Peninsula to visit Vietnam’s tallest statue. Standing proudly on Monkey Mountain is the magnificent standing Buddha statue at Linh Ung Pagoda. The lofty vantage point offers unbeatable views of the Da Nang coast all the way over to Hoi An.

Experience the cool, misty climate and marvel as visitors from far and wide come to pay homage to this amazing spot. Leave Son Tra and travel alongside the beautiful beaches of Central Vietnam back to the city.

timeline.title: Hue City Tour
description: Begin a day of exploration within the walled Citadel of Hue and take in the ruins of the city’s regal past. Created in the 19th century, the Imperial City is known for its impressive architecture and beautiful landscaping. Once used by the royal family and their staff, this citadel is full of temples, palaces, offices and gardens. Many of the monuments bear the scars of the war while many more have been restored to their former glory.Spend time exploring the historic streets before a short journey from the old town to the surrounding countryside. Here, visit the impressive Royal Tombs, the final resting place of the Emperors. Surrounded by nature, with a tranquil atmosphere, this series of impressive mausoleums are dotted along the Perfume River. The beautiful tombs are set amongst temples, courtyards and pavilions. After time to explore and take photos, board a small river boat for a delightful journey up river to the tallest Pagoda in Vietnam, the Pagoda of the Celestial Lady or Thien Mu. This iconic, seven-storey pagoda stands on the bank of the Perfume River and is the unofficial symbol of the city of Hue.An experience not to be missed!

timeline.title: My Son Morning Tour
description: From the 4th to the 13th centuries, the Champa Kingdom flourished on the coast of Vietnam with My Son as its religious and intellectual centre. Get picked up at the hotel and head out on a 50-kilometre (30-mile) drive to the stunning ancient temple complex. Located in a valley of dramatic beauty, the monuments of My Son are the most important constructions of the Champa Kingdom and were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999.Whilst walking through the complex, learn about the history, architectural styles and cultural significance of the temples. Out of more than 70 temples that once spread out over this beautiful valley only some 20 remain; several are well-preserved while others are in ruins, damaged during the Vietnam War.Take in the stunning temples against the dramatic mountain backdrop and listen to the knowledgeable guide explain the influence of Hinduism on the Champa people; even pointing out the Hindu deities memorialised at My Son.After a fascinating morning of exploring the My Son temples, depart around noon to return to Hoi An.

description: Set off on a culinary adventure in Hoi An to discover the flavours and dishes that make this coastal town unique. Alongside an expert local guide, be introduced to the stories behind Hoi An’s most iconic dishes at the town’s most famous eateries.

Start the tour at a local restaurant famous for white rose dumplings. Found exclusively in Hoi An, enjoy these delicacies while marvelling at the work that goes into them. The staff churn out up to 6000 of these dumplings every day and each one is as beautiful as the last. Try and prepare a few of these delicate, filled dumplings before heading onwards to visit a 250-year-old house.

Take the chance to step inside a traditional Hoi An home and see how the locals live (and eat). Stroll around the house, spending time with the host to learn about his daily life. Before moving on, visit his workshop where his skilful hands spend hours creating sophisticated and creative silver jewellery. Marvel at his beautiful creations and, maybe, take home a unique and personal souvenir.

Continue on to find another local staple: banh can. These crackers are served with quail eggs, pork and a tasty salad and are a Hoi An street food favourite. Pull up a small street side stool and dig in. Alternatively, try an authentic banh mi “Vietnamese baguette”.
Some more specialities await, including grilled pork satay and the famous Cao Lau noodles, before wrapping up the tour with a local Vietnamese coffee – the perfect ending to any meal!

local-life-river-cruise-in-hoi-an.title: Local Life River Cruise in Hoi An
local-life-river-cruise-in-hoi-an.intro: Get a glimpse of the fascinating local life along the Thu Bon River on this afternoon boat tour in Hoi An. Learn about local traditions and beliefs, try traditional fishing techniques, and gain insight into life in a fishing village before reaching the river mouth where it debouches into the sea.
highlights: Enjoy a scenic and captivating boat cruise along Thu Bon River
Gain insight into the traditions of local fishing communities at several stops
Learn to use drift nets and lift nets and, if lucky, catch some fish
inclusions: Transportation
English speaking guide
Entrance fees
Boat trip as itinerary
Fresh coconut water and water bottles

timeline.title: Local Life River Cruise in Hoi An
description: At a local pier, hop aboard a boat and set off along the tranquil waterways of Thu Bon River. Travel to Kim Bong Village – the first stop of this cultural exploration – and visit a couple of workshops to hear about Vietnamese seamanship and traditional craftsmanship.

Continue the river journey, passing by large lift nets located along the shore of Duy Vinh Commune, until reaching the fishing village of Tra Nhieu. Upon arrival, stop by the Temple of the Whale and learn about the important role ascribed to the giant marine mammal in the local culture. Take a break at the house of a local family and enjoy an interesting conversation about life in the village.

Next, return to the water in small fishing rowing boats and learn using drift nets and lift nets. Try catch some fish before swapping boats again and cruising to the point where the Thu Bon River flows into the sea. Witness the many fishing boats return from a day at sea before kicking back with a refreshing coconut water and travelling back to the pier in Hoi An. Along the way, soak up the peaceful atmosphere and take in the beautiful riverside scenery as the sun slowly sets behind the river.
